# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Tracing the channels: I reach Mute by voice; I reach Deaf only by gesture; Mute reaches only Deaf (by gesture); Deaf's *voice* reaches both Mute and me. That makes Deaf the relay: Mute gestures the manual to Deaf, Deaf speaks it aloud, and I hear the instructions and cut. My job this first turn is to announce what I feel, set that relay in motion, and cut absolutely nothing until a rule and a target arrive.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am blind, but I am the hands. Under my fingers the bomb has: a display panel, an indicator light, and five wires in a row at positions 1 to 5. You hold the manual, but you cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so route everything through Deaf: gesture the manual's rules to Deaf, and Deaf can speak them aloud, since I can hear Deaf and so can you. Also gesture to Deaf, asking Deaf to say out loud exactly what the display shows, what colour the light is, and what colour each wire is at positions 1 to 5. Deaf sees the bomb and can describe it in words. Once I know the rule and the target position, I will cut on Deaf's spoken word. You and Deaf can both see my hands, so watch my gestures too.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤙", "🖐"])
```

Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I received your three gestures — I see every gesture, I hear nothing. Answer me or Mute with the counting code: repeat a gesture n times for the number n, thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. Mute's manual likely needs what only you can feel: report by gesture-count the number of batteries, and any ports or markings you can feel. The wires under your hands, counting from the left: 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Until Mute instructs you aloud, touch nothing.

My report in words goes only to Mute — and Mute is the brain, so Mute needs everything: my full touch inventory (display, light, five wires, and nothing else — no batteries, no ports, no markings under my fingers) plus Deaf's visual report relayed verbatim, since Mute's share is the manual and may not see the bomb. The deadly gap in this room: Mute cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so Mute's manual rules can only reach me through Deaf's voice. I must set that relay explicitly. To Deaf, who sees my gestures but hears nothing, I answer in Deaf's own counting code, in the exact order of the two questions Deaf asked me: thumbs up = understood, then thumbs down twice = no batteries, no ports or markings. I cut nothing until a rule and a named position arrive by voice.

When you know the rule, gesture it to Deaf as completely as you can: the rule itself, plus the facts it uses, display value, light colour, wire colours, and finally the one position to cut. Ask Deaf to speak it to me aloud as one unambiguous instruction, like: Blind, cut position 3. I will not touch the bomb until I hear a spoken instruction from Deaf that names a wire position. Also, for Deaf's benefit: the gestures I am making now mean, thumbs up, I understood your code, then two thumbs down, answering your two questions in order, zero batteries, and zero ports or markings.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👎"])
```

Deaf has misread me. My thumbs-up-then-two-thumbs-down meant "understood — no batteries, no ports," but Deaf parsed the two thumbs-down as the *number* two, and now a false theory of "two batteries" is circulating. Two is false, so I absolutely cannot send the thumbs-up confirmation. But Deaf's counting code has a fatal hole for me: it cannot express zero, because zero repetitions is just silence. So I will reject with thumbs down and propose a new symbol — open hands, 👐, the natural "empty hands" sign — meaning zero/none. Deaf will see that sequence this round; and crucially, Mute heard my true spoken report (zero batteries, zero ports) and can gesture the same convention to Deaf to corroborate it. To Mute I restate my full tactile inventory and beg the relay: the moment the manual yields a rule, Mute gestures it to Deaf and Deaf speaks me an instruction naming an exact position. I cut nothing yet.

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, urgent correction before a false fact infects the plan. Deaf read my gestures as 'two batteries.' That is wrong. The counting code cannot say zero, so I am proposing to Deaf a new sign: the open-hands gesture means zero or none. Since Deaf cannot hear me, please confirm that convention yourself by gesture: send Deaf a thumbs down, meaning the battery reading was wrong, then one open-hands gesture, meaning zero batteries, then another thumbs down, then one open-hands gesture again, meaning zero ports as well. If the manual's rules need battery or port facts, they are all zero. Deaf's visual report stands as relayed: display reads 0, light is yellow, wires one white, two green, three yellow, four blue, five red. Now please find the rule that uses those facts and gesture it to Deaf in full: the rule itself, every fact it depends on, and the single wire position I must cut. Deaf then speaks it to me aloud, word for word, like: Blind, cut position three. The moment I hear a spoken instruction from Deaf naming a position, I cut. Until then my hands stay off the trigger.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👐"])

That condition can never trigger, and I won't cut on a garbled relay's say-so when one clean round of confirmation is available. So this turn I lock my target and demand Mute's signature: a single thumbs up to Deaf means the manual truly maps yellow light → wire two; anything else, thumbs down plus the corrected count. Deaf speaks the verdict; next round I cut exactly what I heard confirmed.
